extracted.intended_audience: short story writers, editors, and readers interested in anthology selection (esp. PEN/O. Henry submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial reflection on choosing twenty short stories for the PEN/O. Henry Prize Stories anthology; discusses what the series editor looks for (more hopes than fixed criteria) and the mechanics of anonymous juror selection. Useful for writers submitting stories and editors curating anthologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed formal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: I have no set criteria nor do I look for something specific in the many short stories I read each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor explicitly rejects rigid checklists: stories are not required to have certain kinds of characters, settings, plots, nor must they be told using particular voices or styles. The emphasis is on openness rather than adherence to predefined formal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact (be moved)
rubrics_metrics.description: I hope to be moved, for if I feel nothing then what good is all the skill and technique in the world?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional response is primary: a story should move the reader. Technical virtuosity alone is insufficient if the work fails to produce feeling in the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / newness of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: A good story feels new and tells me something I didn't know or makes me aware of something I knew but wouldn't acknowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued are stories that offer fresh insight or reframing — those that reveal previously unrecognized truths or change the reader's awareness. Novelty can be conceptual, emotional, or perceptual rather than merely stylistic innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lasting value / timelessness / re-readability
rubrics_metrics.description: I hope that the stories in each PEN/O. Henry collection will last beyond our momentary political, social, or aesthetic concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for stories likely to endure and reward repeated readings; selections ideally transcend contemporary trends so readers will return to the collection again and again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistry beyond technique
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s my wish to remain an open reader, ready to be astonished and moved, and able to recognize art, which is more than skill and technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition that craft matters but is not the sole determinant: the editor seeks the artistic whole — work that achieves something greater than technical proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial openness / readiness to be astonished
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s my wish to remain an open reader, ready to be astonished and moved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An editorial stance of receptivity: approach submissions without rigid expectations and allow surprising or unexpected works to claim attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to be championed by an individual selector
rubrics_metrics.description: One person has to choose a piece of writing, believe in it, and carry it forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, a chosen story must be one that an individual editor or selector can commit to advocating for — selection often depends on a single person's conviction and willingness to champion the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source/publication is not determinative
rubrics_metrics.description: The world of publishing ... from the most obscure stapled-together journal to a five-minute-old webzine to the most celebrated of book publishers: one person has to choose a piece of writing...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories may be selected regardless of the prestige or visibility of their original publication; quality and the selector's response matter more than the venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymized selection process and independent juror picks
rubrics_metrics.description: Once I’ve gathered them in a manuscript without attribution of authorship or publication, I send the stories to the three jurors of the year. They in turn read them and, without consulting either me or each other, pick an individual favorite and write about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural standard for this anthology: anonymize authorship/publication to focus attention on the work itself; jurors make independent choices and provide written commentary. This implies fairness and an emphasis on individual response rather than consensus metrics.
